title: Fayol's Principles of Management
triggers: one boss for every individual employee
bypass: Hack: Read the case study ending first. If it says 'receive orders from one superior', it's Unity of Command. If it says 'place for everything', it's Order. If it mentions 'promoting team spirit', it's Esprit de Corps. CBSE expects you to quote the exact line from the case study, state the principle, and write a 2-line explanation.

title: Taylor's Scientific Management Techniques
bypass: Hack: Look for the context. 'Eight specialists' = Functional Foremanship. 'Finding one best way' = Method Study. 'Differentiating efficient and inefficient workers' = Differential Piece Wage. Write the name of the technique, its primary objective, and quote the line.
visual_blueprint: Hierarchy tree showing Factory Manager branching into Planning Incharge (4 clerks) and Production Incharge (4 bosses).

title: Steps in the Planning Process
bypass: Hack: Memorize the sequence: 1) Set Objectives, 2) Develop Premises (assumptions about future), 3) Identify Alternatives, 4) Evaluate Alternatives, 5) Select best alternative (Real decision making point), 6) Implement plan, 7) Follow-up. If the case mentions 'assumptions', write 'Developing Premises'.
visual_blueprint: 7-step downward vertical flowchart with arrows connecting each sequential step of planning.

title: Functional vs Divisional Structure
bypass: Hack: If the company makes ONE type of product but has big departments (HR, Sales) -> Functional Structure. If the company makes MULTIPLE products (Cosmetics, Garments, Footwear) -> Divisional Structure. CBSE requires 3 basis of differences (e.g., Formation, Specialization, Responsibility).
visual_blueprint: Comparison table with three columns: Basis, Functional Structure, Divisional Structure.

title: Delegation vs Decentralization
triggers: sharing decision making authority with lower levels
bypass: Hack: Delegation is sharing work with ONE subordinate (routine). Decentralization is a COMPANY-WIDE policy of pushing authority down to the lowest level. Elements of Delegation: Authority (flows down), Responsibility (flows up), Accountability (absolute, cannot be delegated).

title: Internal vs External Sources of Recruitment
bypass: Hack: If company wants 'fresh talent' or 'wider choice', it's External. If they want 'motivation for existing staff' or 'cheaper method', it's Internal (Transfer/Promotion). CBSE always asks for 2 merits and 2 demerits of the chosen source.

title: Selection Process Steps
bypass: Hack: Identify the step currently happening in the case. 1) Preliminary Screening, 2) Selection Tests (Aptitude, Trade, Personality), 3) Employment Interview, 4) Reference Checks, 5) Selection Decision, 6) Medical Exam, 7) Job Offer. You will be asked to state the NEXT 3 steps.
visual_blueprint: Sequential flowchart showing the 7 steps of the Selection Process.

title: Maslow's Need Hierarchy Theory
bypass: Hack: Match the incentive to the need. Pension/Job Security = Safety/Security Needs. Friends/Clubs = Social/Belongingness Needs. Praise/Awards = Esteem Needs. Reaching full potential = Self-Actualization. State the need and how the company satisfied it.
visual_blueprint: A 5-level pyramid starting from Physiological (bottom) to Self-Actualization (top).

title: Leadership Styles
triggers: does not listen to any suggestions
bypass: Hack: Boss gives orders, no discussion = Autocratic (good for factories/unskilled). Boss discusses before deciding = Democratic/Participative. Boss gives full freedom to team = Laissez-Faire/Free-rein (good for highly skilled/scientists).

title: Financial vs Non-Financial Incentives
bypass: Hack: If money is directly/indirectly involved (Bonus, Stock Options, Perks), it's Financial. If it's psychological (Praise, Job Security, Job Enrichment, Participation), it's Non-Financial. Name the incentive and explain it in 2 lines.

title: Controlling Process
bypass: Hack: Sequence is strict. 1) Set Standards, 2) Measure Actual, 3) Compare (Find Deviation), 4) Analyze Deviation, 5) Take Corrective Action. 'Analyzing' has two hacks: Critical Point Control (focus on Key Result Areas) and Management by Exception (ignore minor deviations).
visual_blueprint: 5-step circular flow diagram showing the continuous nature of the Controlling process.

title: Factors Affecting Capital Structure
triggers: mix between owners and borrowed funds
bypass: Hack: Capital Structure = Debt / Equity. More Debt = Higher Financial Risk but higher Earnings Per Share (EPS) if ROI > Cost of Debt (Trading on Equity). Factors to write: Cash Flow Position, Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR), Return on Investment (ROI), Cost of Debt, Tax Rate.

title: Fixed vs Working Capital Decisions
bypass: Hack: Buying machinery/expansion = Fixed Capital (Capital Budgeting). Factors: Scale of operations, Choice of technique. Buying raw materials/credit policy = Working Capital. Factors: Nature of business, Business cycle, Operating cycle length.

title: Dividend Decision Factors
triggers: how much of the profit earned is to be distributed
bypass: Hack: High Growth Company = Low Dividend (retains money). Stable Earnings/Cash Flow = High Dividend. Legal Constraints = Cannot pay dividend from capital. Always list 4 factors with a 1-line explanation for each.

title: Money Market Instruments
bypass: Hack: 'Zero Coupon Bonds' issued by RBI = Treasury Bills. 'Unsecured note by large companies' = Commercial Paper (used for bridge financing/flotation costs). 'Inter-bank lending' = Call Money. Duration is always less than 1 year.

title: Functions of Stock Exchange
bypass: Hack: The core functions are 1) Liquidity (easy to buy/sell), 2) Pricing (demand/supply determines share price), 3) Safety of transaction (regulated by SEBI), 4) Capital formation (savings channeled to industries).

title: Objectives and Functions of SEBI
bypass: Hack: Categorize functions correctly. Protective: Banning insider trading, preventing price rigging. Regulatory: Registering brokers, framing rules. Developmental: Training intermediaries, internet trading. Don't mix up protective and regulatory.

title: Trading Procedure on a Stock Exchange
bypass: Hack: Sequential steps: 1) Select a registered broker, 2) Open Demat Account with a DP, 3) Place order (buy/sell), 4) Execution of order, 5) Issue of Contract Note (contains Unique Order Code), 6) Settlement (T+1 or T+2 rolling settlement).

title: Marketing Philosophies (Concepts)
bypass: Hack: Cheap/mass production = Production Concept. High quality/features = Product Concept. Aggressive ads/discounts = Selling Concept. Finding needs & satisfying them = Marketing Concept. Environment/Society welfare = Societal Marketing Concept.

title: Elements of Marketing Mix (The 4 Ps)
bypass: Hack: The 4 Ps are Product (design, packaging, labeling, branding), Price (cost, demand, competition), Place (channels of distribution, warehousing, inventory), and Promotion (Advertising, Personal Selling, Sales Promotion, Public Relations).
visual_blueprint: A 2x2 grid or 4-petal diagram showing Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.

title: Factors Affecting Price Determination
bypass: Hack: 1) Product Cost sets the minimum price (floor). 2) Utility/Demand sets the maximum price (ceiling). 3) Competition determines where the price lands between floor and ceiling. 4) Government regulations prevent exorbitant pricing of essential goods.

title: Advertising vs Personal Selling
bypass: Hack: Advertising is impersonal, paid, has mass reach, low cost per person, but lacks direct feedback and flexibility. Personal Selling is face-to-face, flexible, provides immediate feedback, but has high cost per person and limited reach.
visual_blueprint: Comparison table with Basis: Form, Flexibility, Reach, Cost per person, and Feedback.

title: Consumer Rights
bypass: Hack: Identify the violation in the case. Electrical shock/danger = Right to Safety. Missing MRP/Expiry date = Right to be Informed. Forcing to buy a combo = Right to Choose. Customer care ignoring complaint = Right to be Heard. Getting refund/replacement = Right to seek Redressal.

title: Consumer Responsibilities
bypass: Hack: If the consumer lost the case in court, they failed a responsibility. Most common fails: Not taking a Cash Memo (Proof of purchase), buying non-standardized goods (No ISI/FPO mark), or not reading expiry dates. List 3-4 responsibilities directly.

title: Consumer Redressal Machinery (Pecuniary Jurisdiction)
triggers: file a complaint in appropriate forum
bypass: Hack: Memorize the limits (as per CPA 2019 limits often tested): District Commission = Claims up to Rs. 1 Crore. State Commission = Claims between Rs. 1 Crore and Rs. 10 Crores. National Commission = Claims above Rs. 10 Crores.
